summary: The equipment is not consistently assembled. Several recent visual upgrades sit on older malformed assemblies; route waypoint tests did not inspect those connections.

findings.title: Checked baggage belts terminate in a solid decorative wall and have no onward system
evidence: Native03_BagDrop01 visibly ends against the timber/solid service wall. Belts point+X, occupy x[-29.7,-26.1] at y-12/-16; check-in east boundary is x-26 and its service lining is near x-26.13/-26.31.

Exports has only two finite bag-drop rectangles and no backstage continuation. airport_journey22.py:70–78 accepts the bag while supported anywhere on the entry belt; no end-of-belt removal/transfer occurs there.
findings.correction: Create proper guarded baggage hatches through ALL overlapping wall/lining layers and a visible short continuation into a supported backstage baggage area. Transfer/sleep bags only after they physically disappear through the guarded hatch. Add guidance distinguishing optional bag drop from security screening.
acceptance: A physical suitcase travels from load point through a real opening without hitting or clipping wall, falling at the end or remaining against it.
The outward transfer is observed over time, not inferred from the accepted flag.
Both belts have consistent arrow direction and accessible stop controls.

findings.title: The emergency stop is embedded in the scanner shoulder
evidence: Source inventory cap local bounds x[.583,.677],y[-.997,-.903],z[.935,1.005]; scanner shoulder extends x[.645,.795] through the same y/z region.
08_ScannerControl shows only a thin yellow fragment behind the body; the red mushroom is obscured.
findings.correction: Move the stop box to an accessible outboard/entry bracket clear of the scanner envelope, with a retained mounting foot and readable emergency-stop identification. Keep the cap circular and above its bezel.
acceptance: The entire cap and guard are visible from the passenger/operator approach.
There is no triangle-volume intersection with scanner body.
The interaction ray reaches the cap/bracket rather than the equipment wall.

findings.title: Right lane side monitor/shelf penetrates the security east partition
evidence: Native machine bounds maxX-35.845; the room east wall is x-36 with interior face near-36.09.
Its side console protrudes about245mm past the interior face at y~2.3, where the wall is solid.
findings.correction: Reposition the entire second screening assembly within the room envelope, including detector, belt, scanner, tray station and targets; do not move only the protruding screen. Preserve both lane clearances and the exit route.
acceptance: All equipment bounds and controls are inside the room with a deliberate service clearance.
Both detectors are walkable and remain aligned with their floor guidance.
Monitor and control interaction rays are unobstructed.

findings.title: Scanner monitor contains a floating weighted foot and conflicting supports
evidence: Old monitor weighted foot bottom is z1.164, while the side work shelf top is1.075: an89mm air gap.
The original articulated support and swivel stem are retained as well. 08_ScannerControl visibly shows a small base hovering above a large shelf.
Terminal34 clones Scanner without excluding original monitor housing/stand; a new readout housing is added over the original enclosure.
findings.correction: Use one coherent support scheme. Prefer a wall/VESA arm with bolted mounting and remove the redundant weighted foot; alternatively seat the foot on the worktop and correctly shorten the stem. Replace overlapping old/new monitor enclosures with one fitted enclosure.
acceptance: Every monitor support member has a continuous mechanical connection to the scanner or shelf.
No horizontal foot floats in air.
Close front/side/rear views show one enclosure and no duplicate protruding backing.

findings.title: A07 desk intersects its room wall
evidence: Native bounds minY-3.055; south room wall is centred y-3 with inside face approximately-2.91.
The desk therefore penetrates the room boundary by~145mm. 27_DeskClearance shows the desk/foot rail crowded against the corner.
findings.correction: Move the complete boarding workstation and its NPC, interaction point, screen/reader and collision proxies north into a planned service bay; preserve a usable staff clearance. Audit A08 and operations workstation similarly rather than applying the move blindly.
acceptance: No desk geometry or support penetrates a wall or adjacent desk.
The staff working area and public scanner approach are both accessible.
The boarding action remains reachable from the public side.

findings.title: A standalone potted plant was left floating when furniture moved
evidence: Native plant base is at[-35.25,.25,1.06], boundsY[.1576,.3424].
The repacking bench now starts at y.533 and the charging table moved to x-32.75. Neither is beneath this plant.
findings.correction: Attach the plant to the new charging surface with its base seated at the actual top height, or relocate it to a real supported ledge. Group props with their supporting furniture so later moves carry them together.
acceptance: Downward support trace from the planter bottom hits its intended furniture within a few millimetres.
The prop does not float or intersect another fixture from any nearby viewpoint.

findings.title: Service-desk carcass and curved front panels are not constructed as a fitted assembly
evidence: The closed carcass has a front face while separate curved doors cross that envelope. The upper outer portions of the door curve reach approximately y-.45 at z.91, behind the carcass front near-.455.
27_DeskClearance shows open dark side voids/strips around the door/end-cheek assembly. The same modeled source is reused at check-in, both gates and operations.

There is no evidence here that the TWO CHECK-IN DESKS mutually intersect: their centres are4m apart and their2.11m widths do not overlap. The verified defects are desk-wall and within-model assembly intersections.
findings.correction: Model an open-front carcass/frame with real backing and shelves, inset doors with consistent reveals, properly joined end cheeks and seated trim. Remove unseen faces behind inset panels instead of layering closed solids. Keep a continuous attached front badge rather than a plaque spanning two functional doors.
acceptance: No front panel crosses the carcass surface in section.
Door reveals are narrow, consistent and backed; no bright/world-visible voids at the ends.
All instances render cleanly at close range while moving.

findings.title: Curtain gaps create an unnecessarily high-contrast high-frequency pattern
evidence: There are12 strips across each tunnel end, width.106m on.112m pitch:6mm bright open gaps.
All curtain parts are static/non-simulating and have zero within-part duplicate faces in the source inventory. That does not prove that no inter-asset overlap exists.
The user image and07_Curtain show the repeated bright lines between very dark strips.
findings.correction: Use a continuous dark interior liner and softly shaped strips/grooves, or realistically stagger the overlaps in depth. Do not widen coplanar front strips into one another, which would create z-fighting. Soften the visible manufactured edges and keep cavity darkness stable.
acceptance: Fixed-camera and moving-camera frame sequences have stable curtain silhouettes and no bright intermittent slit pattern.
Transform samples remain invariant while stationary.
No overlapping coplanar faces are introduced.

findings.title: Stock shelves are populated with identical blank cartons rather than recognizable supplies
evidence: Source inventory:20 identical.18×.17×.30m cartons plus20 plain white rectangular label solids per shelf.
11_StaffStorage confirms the repeated five colours and blank labels.
findings.correction: Create a small coherent supply set with recognizable silhouettes and readable role labels: folded blankets, first-aid packs, radio/headset cases, document binders and boxed service supplies. Vary arrangement according to staff storage versus gallery retail; retain a consistent smooth stylized finish.
acceptance: At normal player distance each product family is identifiable without zoom.
There are meaningful shape/material differences and labels, not only recolours.
Every item rests on a shelf with no wall intersection.

findings.title: Shelf price rails float in front of the shelves
evidence: Shelf front y-.245; rail back y-.258, leaving13mm unsupported air.
Four rails are simple6-face boxes with no clips/attachment geometry.
findings.correction: Seat the rails directly on the shelf edge or add actual retained clips. If used in staff storage, replace retail price rails with appropriate inventory tags.
acceptance: The rail back contacts its support continuously or at modeled clips.
Close oblique views show no floating horizontal strip.

findings.title: Legacy recycling units have painted-on recesses instead of apertures
evidence: The source consists of a closed housing, door and dark solid rectangles named Open dark recess; there is no cut-out or open liner.
Newer café Bins36 already use genuine openings, so the map contains inconsistent prop construction standards.
findings.correction: Replace the legacy units with a compact genuinely open version, including a liner, thickness and either a swing flap or an actual mouth. Keep a clear label appropriate to location.
acceptance: A view into the aperture shows a supported dark cavity rather than the outside floor or a flat solid decal.
No open shell backfaces or floating trim are visible.

findings.title: Screening tray stacks remain on the floor rather than the preparation worktop
evidence: Both stacks are at scannerX,y.8, baseZ0,.12,.24,.36, whereas the supported preparation worktop is aroundz.94.
They are nonblocking decorative instances, with no coherent tray-use journey.
findings.correction: Put the stack on a fitted waist-height input cart or the preparation bench and make the equipment layout communicate prepare→load→walk→collect. Add a receiving shelf at the output or bounded return arrangement.
acceptance: All trays rest on a support, with a deliberate reachable input/collection position.
The route cannot be mistaken for putting belongings on the floor.
If trays are interactive, they can be picked up and placed without slipping through the surface.

findings.title: The fitted café run has100mm open voids between cabinet bases
evidence: Each base/plinth is1.90m wide while counters are placed2.0m apart; worktops are2.0m wide.
24_CafeService visibly exposes100mm vertical gaps between base units below the almost-continuous worktop. The units have separate backs, so the service void is not closed by a continuous rear panel.
findings.correction: Model scribed filler panels/pilasters and continuous plinth/backing at the three joints, or author the run as one fitted cabinet frame with separate functional doors. Retain honest narrow worktop joints.
acceptance: Front and oblique views show a continuous backed run with no view through100mm gaps.
Doors, pulls and plaques do not intersect the fillers.
All four equipment stations remain accessible.

not_proven: No proof that the scanner itself physically moves; native scanner is static. Motion/temporal causes require frame/transform analysis.
No proof of mutually overlapping check-in desks in current placements.
AP COLL proxy component visible flags do not establish that actors render: actor hidden-in-game must also be checked.
coverage: Bag-drop input, conveyor direction, wall termination and runtime acceptance
Both security portals, belts, scanners, curtains, controls, monitor supports and trays
Gate A07/A08 and operations workstation construction/placement
Trolleys, reclaim carousel and extinguisher source inventories
